blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Drivers of Transport Network Vehicle Service (TNVS) units operating under the so-called “tempo” status have been given an additional 30 days to apply for regularization, the Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB) said Friday, November 6. The extension gives TNVS drivers more time to secure authorization for their vehicles, which transport network companies (TNCs) had allowed onto their platforms before they obtained the necessary authority from the LTFRB. Known in the transport sector as “tempo,” the practice violates LTFRB regulations because it allows unauthorized vehicles to offer public transport services through ride-hailing platforms.
